This article compares the procedure codes assigned to echocardiography within the Danish National Health Service Register (Sygesikringsregisteret), based on a 2023 registry snapshot [^src1]. The comparison highlights how the register categorizes cardiac ultrasound procedures using specific numerical identifiers, ranging from general codes to highly specialized examination types [^src1].

The lowest numerical code in this set is [[2208-ekkocardiografi|2208 Ekkocardiografi]], which serves as a broad, unspecified designation for the procedure [^src1]. The registry also employs the 3800-series to stratify the complexity of the examination: [[3810-ekkocardiografi-standardundersoegelse|3810 Ekkocardiografi, standardundersøgelse]] is designated for standard examinations, whereas [[3811-ekkocardiografi-avanceret-undersoegelse|3811 Ekkocardiografi, avanceret undersøgelse]] is used for advanced procedures [^src1]. 

The highest numerical codes belong to the 5100-series, which captures specialized modalities [^src1]. These include [[5101-ekko-cardiografi|5101 EKKO-cardiografi]], [[5102-transsofageal-ekko|5102 Transsøfofagal ekko.]] for transesophageal approaches, and [[5103-stress-ekkocardiogra|5103 Stress ekkocardiogra]] for stress tests [^src1]. As an outlier in data formatting, the descriptions for codes 5102 and 5103 contain apparent truncations or punctuation anomalies (e.g., ending in a period or cutting off at "ekkocardiogra"), which likely reflects legacy character limits or data entry artifacts in the register's database [^src1]. 

Because this data is drawn from a single dated section, no longitudinal trends regarding the adoption, frequency, or retirement of these codes can be established [^src1].
